description.narrative: The development objective of the Enhancing Systematic Land Registration Project for Lao, Peoples Democratic Republic (PDR) is to support the Government of Lao PDR in improving tenure security and land administration services in selected areas, and to provide immediate and effective response in case of an eligible crisis or emergency. The project comprises of five components. The first component, systematic registration of land use rights will support the Government of Lao PDR (GOL), Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MONRE), and Department of Lands (DOL) in enhancing and scaling-up systematic land registration and issuance of 1,000,000 land titles and use certificates outside state forestlands in all 18 provinces of Lao PDR. It consists of following sub-components: (i) scaling-up systematic land registration; and (ii) training and capacity building. The second component, modernization of land administration and service delivery will support the GOL, MONRE, and DOL in improving the delivery of land administration services (surveying, registration, transactions, subdivisions, etc.). It consists of following sub-components: (i) enhanced service delivery; (ii) scanning, digitization, and archiving of existing land records; and (iii) Lao landreg development and rollout. The third component, implementation, policy and legal framework development will support the further development of inclusive and comprehensive land policies and regulatory framework, as well as their implementation procedures. The fourth component, project management will support overall project management and coordination. The fifth component, contingent emergency response component (CERC) will provide immediate response to an eligible emergency, as needed.

The objective of the project is to support the Government of Lao PDR in improving tenure security and land administration services in selected areas, and to provide immediate and effective response in case of an eligible crisis or emergency.

title.narrative: Number of annual land transactions registered, excluding first time registration (disaggregated by transfers, mortgages, leases and inheritance; disaggregated by gender)

comment.narrative:
The indicator measures the annual number of subsequent land transactions in Lao PDR. The data is disaggregated by transfer, mortgages, leases and inheritance. The disaggregated information will eventually be available directly from Lao LandReg but for now is conducted manually via reviewing logbooks at each of the 18 PONRE offices. The baseline data is based on 2019 information from all provinces, except Phongsaly, Luangnamtha, Khammouane and Salavan due to lack of data provided to central level.
From January to December 2024, there were a total of 39,427 transactions, which includes 19,808 sales, 12,594 mortgages, 1,925 inheritances, 5,011 transfers and 89 leases out of which 58.36% were in the name of women. The majority of provinces reported increases in land transactions; however, the decrease in transfers was caused by substantial drops in transactions reported by two large provinces-Vientiane Capital City and Luang Prabang.

title.narrative: Land titles or use certificates issued by the project in selected areas (disaggregated by titles/certificates, gender and ethnicity) (Number)

comment.narrative: This indicator will measure the number of properties and land parcels in Lao PDR that have received land title or use certificate. Land titles and use certificates are considered to be issued when they are prepared and printed, regardless if the land holder collects them from DONRE or not. The disaggregated information will be reported in the progress reports. The disaggregated information on titles/certificates and gender is available in Lao LandReg, while disaggregated information on ethnicity must be collectedhrough other means, such as reports of the mobile units or DONREs. The ethnicity information is not expected to be collected in the first year of project implementation.

title.narrative: Land titles or use certificates issued by the project in selected areas (disaggregated by titles/certificates, gender and ethnicity) (Number)

comment.narrative:
This indicator measures the number of properties and land parcels in Lao PDR that have received land titles or use certificates. The indicator was revised during restructuring in February 2024 to capture solely titles issued by the project and not all land titles issued by GoL. Accordingly, the baseline was reset to 0 and the target revised to 650,000.
As of September 2025, 71% of titles have been issued to women including individual, conjugal and joint titles. 18% of titles have been issued to landowners of ethnic minority groups.

title.narrative: Coverage of cadastral index maps showing all land holdings, including communal lands, prepared by the project in selected areas.

comment.narrative:
This indicator shows the coverage of the cadastral index maps prepared in the project. Communal land refers to state land for collective use. In the February 2024 restructuring, this indicator was revised to only include hectares mapped by the Project. Accordingly the end target was reset to 1,484,517 ha.
An updated calculation was done in December 2024. According to the central Lao LandReg database, the average plot size in ESLRP target areas is 1.58 hectares (comprising around 2/3 agriculture land use and 1/3 construction land). With a total of 209,897 surveyed land plots by December 2024, the total coverage of cadastral index maps computes to 331,637 hectares.

title.narrative: Coverage of cadastral index maps showing all land holdings, including communal lands, prepared by the project in selected areas.

comment.narrative:
This indicator shows the coverage of the cadastral index maps prepared in the project.The target was originally estimated using 2.28 hectares per parcel. As part of the February 2024 restructuring, this indicator was revised to only include hectares mapped by the Project. Accordingly, the endline target was reset to 1,484,517 ha. In December 2024, the central Lao LandReg database showed the average plot size in ESLRP target area was 1.58 hectares (comprising around 2/3 agricultural land use and 1/3 construction land). It was estimated that the average plot size would remain approximately the same until the project's completion, projecting the total index map coverage of 650,000 land plots to reach approximately 773,500 hectares. Hence in a second restructuring in June 2025, the target was lowered to 770,000 hectares.
With a total of 289,644 surveyed land plots by September 2025, the total coverage of cadastral index maps computes to 457,637 hectares.

title.narrative: Number of old paper land records scanned, linked to Lao LandReg and archived.

comment.narrative:
This indicator measures the number of land titles or use certificates that are scanned, linked to the land parcel in Lao LandReg and archived. During restructuring, the baseline was corrected to 0 and target to 441,000. In August 2024, a company was contracted to conduct scanning and digitization in Vientiane Capital.
As of September 2025, scanning was completed for 437,541 land plots, with data capture conducted for around 95,000 plots. Although all PDF scans have been linked to the LandReg production database via an API, data entries for the 95,000 parcels remain in a clone database with 0 parcels in Lao LandReg.

title.narrative: Beneficiaries who participate in public awareness campaigns (disaggregated by ethnicity)

comment.narrative:
This indicator measures the percentage of beneficiaries participating in project public awareness campaigns out of the total number of households, as well as provides the percentage that are ethnic. This indicator was restructured in February 2024. The baseline was set to 0 instead of 50% as the public awareness campaigns for ESLRP began in 2023. The indicator target was revised to 33.3% instead of 50% to reflect that often only 1 person per extended family (multiple households) attends the public awareness campaigns.
By June 2025, a total of 58,483 individuals attended public awareness campaigns, reaching 38.8% of the 150,786 households across 755 villages. Of all participants, 15,152 were from ethnic minority groups, accounting for 25.9% of overall attendance.

title.narrative: Average cost of issuance of new land title

comment.narrative:
This indicator measures the average cost of issuing a new land title. Baseline was set at 25 dollars based on a GIZ study. This analysis covers costs related to investments, training, and daily operations.
According to this approach, the current cost per land title stood at $66.40 in September 2024, while the average cost per surveyed land plot in ESLRP stood at $25.72. The difference was due to the current backlog of issued land title versus plot surveyed. Furthermore, the average costs per plot or land title driven by the relatively high initial investment, as the land registration activities had been underway for less than two years. By September 2025, the average cost per land titles has further reduced to $28.84, from previously $30.80 in December 2024.

title.narrative: Average cost of issuance of new land title

comment.narrative:
This indicator measures the average cost of issuing a new land title. Baseline was set at 25 dollars based on a GIZ study. This analysis covers costs related to investments, training, and daily operations.
By December 2024, a strong increase in the number of issued land titles led to a significant reduction in cost, bringing the average down to $30.80 per issued land title.

title.narrative: Districts with digital land information system (Lao LandReg) operational and in systematic use

comment.narrative: This tracks the roll-out of Lao LandReg Version 7 which processes first time registration and subsequent transactions. The baseline was formed by the districts of Houaphan, Luang Namtha and Xayaboury, which were the first provinces where Lao LandReg was initially introduced for processing first time registrations. In 2024, GIZ piloted Lao LandReg Version 6 in Houaphan (10 Districts) and Xayaboury (11 Districts) but was no longer working with Luang Namtha. In Feb 2025, ESLRP piloted LaoLandReg Version 7 in Vientiane Capital (9 Districts), reaching an overall number of 30 Districts. Previous reporting incorrectly included Luang Namtha's 5 Districts. By Sep 2025, ESLRP rolled out Lao LandReg Version 7 in 6 more provinces: Vientiane Province (11 districts), Luang Prabang (12 districts), Khammouane (10 districts), Savannakhet (15 districts), Champasak (10 districts) and in October 2025 to another 3 provinces: Luang Namtha (5 Districts), Bolikhamxay (7 Districts) and Oudomxay (7 Districts).

title.narrative: Districts with digital land information system (Lao LandReg) operational and in systematic use

comment.narrative: Baseline was formed by the districts of Houaphan, Luang Namtha and Xaignabouly which regularly update data from the provincial to central level database. Since then, 9 districts in VCC have piloted Lao LandReg v7.2. The figure remained unchanged but is expected to rise as Lao LandReg V7.2 rolls out this year.

title.narrative: Income generation to government through DOL (excluding first registration fees) in Lao Kip

comment.narrative:
This indicator measures amount of annual income generated to the government by DOL through land administration fees excluding first-time registration fees. It was restructured in February 2024 from US$ to Kip due to the drastic change in exchange rate (from 9,170 at baseline to over 20,000), as well as removing the LAK 747,362,000 out of LAK 779,492,650 million from the baseline which was capital gains tax and hence not DOL income. Baseline was hence reset to LAK32,131,000 to count only DOL income.
2022 income was LAK 56,715,639 while 2023 income was LAK 38,896,339.2024. In 2024 DOL reported income of LAK 91,400,000. The increase is due to additional income from leasing the CORs established by the Project.

title.narrative: Time taken to register a land transaction

comment.narrative: The indicator measures the days taken to conduct a land transfer based on Lao LandReg from application to approval. This indicator was part of restructuring, replacing the data source with Lao LandReg instead of WB's Doing Business indicator which is no longer being published and was based on a transfer of an already registered commercial parcel. The baseline was set to 55 days based on the average time to conduct a land transfer over 3 years (2020, 2021 and 2022) according to data available in Lao LandReg. Follow-up data will be provided following the rollout of Lao LandReg v 7.2.
